title: Duane (Keffe D) Davis sentenced to 40 years to life in prison for murder of rapper Tupac Shakur
summary: Duane (Keffe D) Davis received a sentence of to 40 years to life in prison Tuesday for orchestrating the murder of rap icon Tupac Shakur, who was gunned down off the Las Vegas Strip over 30 years ago.

image.caption: Duane Davis, right, and his attorney Michael Sanft are seen in a Las Vegas courtroom in August after a jury found Davis guilty of first-degree murder in the 1996 killing of rapper Tupac Shakur. (Bizuayehu Tesfaye/Las Vegas Review-Journal/Associated Press)

blocks.text: World·Updated

Duane (Keffe D) Davis received a sentence of to 40 years to life in prison Tuesday for orchestrating the murder of rap icon Tupac Shakur, who was gunned down off the Las Vegas Strip over 30 years ago.
Shakur's siblings spoke during Tuesday's sentencing
· The Associated Press
· Posted: Oct 13, 2026 11:26 AM EDT | Last Updated: 23 minutes ago
Davis was convicted in August of first-degree murder with the use of a deadly weapon. He is the only person ever charged in the death of Shakur, whose popularity was peaking at age 25.
Prosecutor Marc DiGiacomo had said during Tuesday's sentencing that whatever sentence the court imposes, the 63-year-old Davis is "guaranteed to die" behind bars.
The killing went unsolved for years until Davis, a former leader of the South Side Compton Crips, gave interviews and published his role in the shooting in his 2019 tell-all memoir.
DiGiacomo said Davis was trying to profit off a killing that he committed, and for that "in my mind, he deserves the maximum possible sentence."
Sekyiwa Shakur and Maurice Shakur, two of the rapper's siblings, spoke during the hearing.

Davis also spoke briefly in court, telling Judge Carli Kierny he wants items back that police took from his house, including his pictures. Asked if there was anything else he wanted to say, Davis said: "No, I'm good."
Davis's lawyer, Michael Sanft, said he plans to appeal the verdict. Sanft said prosecutors waited too long to bring the case.

On the night of Sept. 7, 1996, Shakur was in the passenger seat of a black BMW with music mogul Marion (Suge) Knight when a white Cadillac pulled up at a red light and shots erupted. Shakur was shot multiple times and died six days later, while Knight survived.

Shakur is considered one of the most influential and versatile rappers of all time and had a burgeoning film career as an actor at the time of his death. His legend has only grown since. His songs still resonate among fans with themes of hardship, love and Black struggles.
Duane Davis found guilty in murder of Tupac Shakur | Hanomansing Tonight

In his memoir, Davis explained how Shakur and his entourage beat up Davis's nephew hours before the shooting in Las Vegas. He said he sought retaliation, and that he was in the passenger seat of the Cadillac and passed the gun to the back seat, where shots were fired. Davis had spoken to detectives years before but avoided prosecution because of an agreement he made with law enforcement.

During the weekslong trial, prosecutors relied on Davis's own statements he made to law enforcement and documentarians. They argued Davis orchestrated the shooting and provided the gun used in Shakur's death, which was the result of a rivalry between the South Side Compton Crips and Mob Piru.

Davis's defence attorney pointed to a lack of physical evidence that connected his client to the 30-year-old crime, and he portrayed Davis as a liar who was trying to make money. After nine days of hearing testimony in August, the jury deliberated for three hours before turning over the guilty verdict.
Davis said in court that he plans to appeal.
Rap icon also 'a brother, a son'
Shakur's family is expected to speak at the sentencing, including his siblings Maurice (Mopreme) Shakur and Sekyiwa (Set) Shakur.

Fans of Tupac Shakur hold up a painted portrait of late rapper and actor as they stand with others during a 2023 ceremony honouring him with a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame in Los Angeles. (Chris Pizzello/Invision/Associated Press)

Following the verdict, prosecutor Binu Palal said that to many people, Shakur was an icon or an idea, "but to the family, Tupac Shakur was a brother, a son, a cousin, a loved person ripped from them 30 years ago."
Palal said the family had to sit through years of Davis "bragging about killing someone they loved."
"They loved that man. And the arrogance that Mr. Davis had in expressing his joy in killing that man ultimately was his undoing," Palal said.

Davis is the only person to be charged and convicted in the killing of Shakur. The three other people who allegedly were in the Cadillac — including Davis's nephew Orlando (Baby Lane) Anderson, who Davis said was the one who pulled the trigger — have died.
'Insufficient evidence' for more charges: prosecutors
Sean (Diddy) Combs and his alleged role were brought up often throughout the trial. Witnesses testified Combs used members of the South Side Compton Crips for security for Bad Boy Records.

In his book and public statements, Davis alleged Combs offered him money to kill Shakur and Knight. Combs, who is serving a four-year prison sentence after being convicted of prostitution-related offences, has repeatedly denied any involvement in the death of Shakur.
Clark County district attorney Steve Wolfson has said his office doesn't believe it has sufficient evidence to charge anyone else.
"But like any other case, if we come into more information, more evidence, we can always consider filing additional charges," he said following the guilty verdict.
"But today, we don't believe that's the appropriate move to make."
